intent: calculate and interpret odds implied probability
title: Implied probability is a price, not the truth
description: Convert American or decimal odds to implied probability, remove a simple two-way margin, and understand why no-vig probability is still not objective truth.
dek: Odds can be translated into a probability-shaped price. That calculation is useful, but it does not reveal the unknowable true chance of an outcome by itself.
author: chris-habib

hero.alt: A probability curve, percentage arc, and odds tile aligned on a green calibration grid
hero.caption: AI-assisted editorial illustration. The diagram is conceptual and does not show a real market or result.

disclosure: This guide explains price mathematics for research and education. A no-vig calculation is a normalization method, not proof of a true probability or a profitable opportunity.
verdict: Use implied probability to put prices on a common scale. Use no-vig probability to remove a simple form of bookmaker margin. Call neither number true probability without an independent, well-tested estimate and a clear account of uncertainty.

faqs.question: How do I convert positive American odds to implied probability?
faqs.answer: For positive odds A, divide 100 by A plus 100. At +120, 100 divided by 220 equals 45.45 percent raw implied probability.

faqs.question: How do I convert negative American odds to implied probability?
faqs.answer: For negative odds, use the absolute value A and divide A by A plus 100. At -150, 150 divided by 250 equals 60 percent raw implied probability.

faqs.question: Is no-vig probability the same as true probability?
faqs.answer: No. A proportional no-vig calculation removes the displayed margin by normalizing all outcomes to 100 percent. It does not prove that the market allocated margin evenly or reveal an objective true probability.
